fields.description: Shown under the workspace in this app's sidebar, and as the browser tab's title. Left blank it reads Commons.
fields.label: Title

fields.description: Shows each Date and Datetime field's value in Bikram Sambat beside it, and offers a Bikram Sambat calendar for picking one. Dates are still stored in the Gregorian calendar. Takes effect when each user reloads the page.
fields.label: Enable Bikram Sambat Calendar

fields.description: Where /commons opens. Left blank, it opens the first page in the person's sidebar that they may use.
fields.label: Landing Page
fields.options:
Announcements
Account Balance
Leave Request
Expense Claim
Procurement
Attendance
Bank Reconciliation
Document Capture

fields.description: Changes to how people find their way around, in the desk and in Commons alike. Like the Core Overrides, these change how Frappe itself behaves and lean on details of its code that an upgrade can change without warning, so they are the first to switch off if navigation misbehaves after an upgrade. Changes to the desk take effect when each user reloads the page.

Turns Frappe's Dock, the column left of the desk's sidebar, into a rail of apps rather than the open app's modules: the Navigation Apps configured here, then every installed app for the modules those leave unclaimed. Picking an app shows its module list in the sidebar (its frontend first, then its modules under the Categories its Navigation App sets); picking it again from inside a module shows the list again. An app with one module opens it. The menu at the top of the sidebar also lists the open app's modules, the header names the module over its app, and the mark at the top of the rail opens the Apps screen. Search and Notifications move from the top of the sidebar to the foot of the rail. Applies to the desk; the Commons frontend does not have the rail yet. Suspect this first if the rail or the sidebar's top menu are missing entries or open the wrong page.
fields.label: Enable Navigation Rail

fields.description: In the desk, moves the site's tools (the Navbar Settings rows, such as System Console) and Help from the menu at the top of the sidebar into the user menu (your avatar at the foot of the rail, or of the sidebar), above Logout. In Commons, opens a menu from your name at the foot of the sidebar, holding your account, display, session defaults, site tools, help and logout. Suspect this first if either menu is missing entries or does not open.
fields.label: Enable User Menu

fields.description: Uses each Role's Home Page Priority to decide where someone holding several roles lands after logging in: the lowest number wins. Without it, Frappe uses the first role the database happens to return. Suspect this first if people land on the wrong page after logging in, or opening the site root goes somewhere unexpected.
fields.label: Enable Home Page Priority

fields.description: Adds a To Do button beside the notification bell, opening your open ToDos with a count of them in a drawer like the Notifications one: in the sidebar's top rows, or at the foot of the navigation rail when that is on (where both drawers open beside the rail). The Commons frontend has its own To Do panel either way. Suspect this first if the To Do button or its drawer misbehaves.
fields.label: Enable Desk To Do

fields.description: Arranges Frappe's Apps screen (/desk, with Desktop Settings on Apps) from the Navigation Apps, in rail order: each app as one icon, as an icon per module, or not at all, as its Apps Screen setting says. Apps with no Navigation App show as one icon, and apps taken off the rail are left off. Turning this off brings back Frappe's own Apps screen. Suspect this first if the Apps screen is missing an app or a module.
fields.label: Enable Apps Screen from Navigation Apps

fields.options: Opt-in features that change how Frappe and its apps behave, not just what Commons adds on top of them. They depend on details of code that an upgrade can change without warning. If something stops working the way it should, especially just after an upgrade, try switching the matching one off first. Changes to the desk take effect when each user reloads the page.

fields.description: Keeps @ unescaped in desk addresses, so a record named after an email address reads /desk/member/name@example.org rather than /desk/member/name%40example.org. Suspect this first if moving between desk pages leaves extra entries in the Back button's history, or opens the wrong record.
fields.label: Enable Literal @ in Desk URLs

fields.description: Lets desk pages show screens from this app's own frontend, such as Bank Reconciliation at /desk/commons-banking, Document Capture at /desk/commons-capture and the attendance register at /desk/commons-attendance. It installs, on this version of Frappe, the way of doing this that the next version of Frappe will ship (desk islands). Nothing is stored, so switching this off loses nothing; the pages then point to the same screens under /commons. Suspect this first if a desk page drawn by this app is blank or its dialogs misbehave.
fields.label: Enable Desk Islands

fields.description: Adds a Require User Permission checkbox to the Role Permission Manager. A role with it ticked sees no records until a User Permission narrows it, and cannot run Query or Script Reports on that doctype. Unticking this WIDENS ACCESS: those roles fall back to Frappe's own rules and see every record their permissions grant, and the checkbox disappears from the Role Permission Manager. The ticks are kept, and take effect again when this is ticked. Suspect this first if users get empty lists, or 'Not permitted' on documents and reports their roles should reach.
fields.label: Enable Require User Permission Gate

fields.description: Lets a Custom Field show a value read live from a linked record, through its Derived From property, instead of storing a copy. Nothing is stored, so switching this off loses no data; derived fields simply read as empty. Suspect this first if lists, reports or forms of a doctype with derived fields start failing or showing wrong values.
fields.label: Enable Derived Docfields

fields.description: Adds a Visual view to the email composer whenever it holds an HTML email, such as one from an MJML template: the email as it will look, with its text editable in place and its layout left alone. The HTML view is still one click away. Suspect this first if the composer misbehaves while writing an HTML email.
fields.label: Enable Visual HTML Email Editor

fields.description: What ERPNext, HRMS and Lending write to the books. Each says which documents it reaches.
fields.label: Accounting

fields.description: Puts a Payment Entry's own party on its tax and deduction lines to Payable accounts, such as TDS, so that each withholding is kept against the party it was withheld from and shows in Accounts Payable. Without it ERPNext leaves those lines without a party, and then refuses to submit them. The party is added where ERPNext first builds the ledger lines, so cancelling, reconciling and reposting the payment all undo the rows it made; a GL Entry server script that sets the party instead leaves a cancelled payment on Accounts Payable. Affects payments submitted, cancelled or reposted while it is on. Suspect this first if a payment's ledger lines name a party they should not.
fields.label: Enable Party on Payable Payment Lines

fields.description: Splits a payroll run's accrual journal into one line per employee for each earnings and deduction account, each with the employee's department from their salary slip, and with the employee as party on Payable accounts such as TDS. HRMS's own totals are kept: a line whose employees' parts do not add up to HRMS's total is posted as HRMS's single line and an error is logged. Payroll Payable is split per employee by Payroll Settings' Process Payroll Accounting Entry Based on Employee, which should be on as well; this adds the department to those lines. Only the accrual journal is changed, and only for runs whose accrual is made while this is on. Suspect this first if a payroll run will not submit or its journal's lines look wrong.
fields.label: Enable Payroll Lines per Employee

fields.description: With Payroll Settings' Process Payroll Accounting Entry Based on Employee on, an employee's Payment Entry may settle their salary on a payroll run, and a submitted Payroll Entry gets Create Payment Entries: a draft Payment Entry for each employee the run still owes. This is the Mode of Payment that dialog starts on, and whose default account for the company it pays from when the run names no payment account. Blank starts it on none.
fields.label: Payroll Payment Mode of Payment

fields.description: The Reference No the Create Payment Entries dialog starts on, for a site that pays every run under one reference. Blank starts it empty. ERPNext requires a Reference No on a payment from a bank account, so the dialog asks for one when it pays from a Bank account.
fields.label: Payroll Payment Reference

fields.description: Clears a Journal Entry on its own posting date when it moves no money at the bank: every bank and cash account on it nets to nothing, as when money moves between two departments that share one bank account. No bank statement will carry a line for such an entry, so without this it waits in Bank Clearance and the Bank Reconciliation Statement until it is cleared by hand. An entry that also moves money on another bank account is left to be cleared as usual, and one that already has a clearance date keeps it. Ticking this also clears, once, the submitted entries of this kind that are still waiting. Suspect this first if a journal entry is cleared that should not be.
fields.label: Enable Clearing Internal Transfers

fields.description: Books a Loan Repayment, Loan Write Off or Loan Disbursement on its own date: the posting date entered on a repayment, the value date of a write-off, the disbursement date of a disbursement. Without it lending dates them, and their GL, on the day they are saved, so one entered after the fact sits in the books on the wrong day. It also keeps the repayments after a backdated one on their own dates when lending reposts them, which it otherwise books on the day of the repost. On a disbursement with a monthly schedule and no first repayment date, the first repayment then counts from the disbursement date. Affects vouchers saved or reposted while it is on; the Loan Date Audit lists those booked before. Suspect this first if a lending voucher's ledger is dated other than lending would date it.
fields.label: Enable Loan Vouchers on Their Own Dates

fields.description: How ERPNext's financial reports read the books back out. Neither changes what is in them.
fields.label: Financial Reports

fields.description: Gives a financial report filtered by Fiscal Year one column per fiscal year, from that year's own start date to its own end date and headed with its name. Without it ERPNext steps twelve calendar months from the first year's start and never asks where each year ends, so years that do not end on a month's last day, such as Bikram Sambat years, come out a day off, with an extra one-day column at the end that repeats the one before it. Monthly, quarterly and half-yearly columns also stay inside their year, and a stub of less than a week at a year's end joins the column before it. Reaches Profit and Loss, the Balance Sheet, Cash Flow and every other report that lays periods out as columns; a Date Range filter keeps ERPNext's own columns, as do years that do not follow one another day after day. Suspect this first if a report's columns are not the ones ERPNext would draw.
fields.label: Enable Fiscal Year Columns

fields.description: Adds a Hide Internal Accounts filter to Profit and Loss and the Gross and Net Profit Report. Ticked, it leaves out each Account with Internal Account ticked, and every account under one that is a group, before anything is added up, so the totals and net profit are those of what is left. Net profit only stays the same when the internal income and expense net to nothing. Nothing is hidden until the filter is ticked on the report itself, and Report Templates are not reached. Suspect this first if those reports' totals differ from the General Ledger's.
fields.label: Enable Hiding Internal Accounts

fields.description: Without a Workflow, an expense claim that names no approver can be decided by anyone who may submit Expense Claims, who is then recorded as its approver. Unticked, such a claim waits until someone names an approver, as in HRMS.
fields.label: Let Any Approver Decide Unassigned Claims

fields.description: How a Record Change Request is decided on a site that runs no Workflow for it. With a Workflow, the Workflow decides all of this.
fields.label: Record Change Requests

fields.description: The status, one of the doctype's own Status options, that writes the proposed values to the record.
fields.label: Outcome That Applies the Change

fields.description: Unticked, a reviewer cannot decide a request they raised themselves.
fields.label: Allow Deciding Your Own Request

fields.description: A Link or Data field of Procurement Request the approvals queue is grouped by, each group with its estimated total. Blank: one list.
fields.label: Group Approvals By

fields.description: The fields a site has added to Education's doctypes for what Education has no field for. Each is the fieldname of a field on that doctype; left blank, the register at /commons/attendance does without it.
fields.label: Marks

fields.description: A Check field on Student Attendance marking a student present but late. Blank: the register offers no Late mark.
fields.label: Late Arrival Field

fields.description: The share of a session's hours a late arrival earns, from 0 to 1. 1 counts it as fully present.
fields.label: Late Arrival Credit

fields.description: What Education's Leave status counts as. Absent: the session counts against the student like any absence. Excused: the session is left out of that student's total, both the hours earned and the hours possible.
fields.label: Leave Counts As

fields.description: A Data or Select field on Course Schedule naming the kind of session. The register groups and totals by it. Blank: no grouping by type.
fields.label: Session Type Field

fields.description: A text field on Course Schedule describing the session, shown and edited beside it.
fields.label: Session Details Field

fields.description: A Float or Int field on Course Schedule holding the hours a session is worth. Where a session has a value above 0, it is used instead of the time between its start and end. Blank: hours come from the times.
fields.label: Session Hours Field

fields.description: A Check field on Academic Term retiring a term. Ticked terms are left out of the register. Blank: every term is offered.
fields.label: Inactive Term Field

fields.description: How a course finds its student groups for a term. Programme: groups whose programme teaches the course (Program Course). Course: course-based groups naming the course themselves. Both: either.
fields.label: Find Student Groups By

fields.description: A table on Course listing the kinds of session the course is taught in and the hours planned for each. The register offers a course's own kinds first when a session is timetabled, and shows planned hours beside scheduled ones. Blank: every kind already used is offered, and no hours are planned.
fields.label: Course Plan

fields.description: A Table field on Course.
fields.label: Course Plan Table

fields.description: The column of that table naming the kind of session, in the same words as the Session Type Field.
fields.label: Session Type Column

fields.description: The Float or Int column of that table holding the planned hours.
fields.label: Planned Hours Column

fields.description: The Data Sync page (/desk/commons-data-sync) compares this site's configuration with a source site, usually a development copy of it, and copies changes here one record at a time. Your browser reads the source, so it only has to be reachable from where you open the page.
fields.label: Source

fields.description: The source site's address as your browser reaches it, for example http://mysite.localhost:8000. The source must allow this site's origin: bench --site <source> set-config allow_cors "https://this.site".
fields.label: Source Site URL

fields.description: Compared and copied in this order, so list a doctype after what it depends on: Custom Fields before the Property Setters that change them. Empty: the defaults, which cover site-made customisation.
fields.label: Tracked Doctypes
